approachNotice: Follow one worked approach; other approaches can also be valid.

patterns.label: Direct scan or simulation
patterns.summary: Visit the needed input positions or carry out the listed operations in order.

patterns.label: Hash map or set
patterns.summary: Use keys to look up stored values or counts; use a set to test whether a value has been seen.

patterns.label: Two pointers
patterns.summary: Track two positions or node references and move them according to the values being compared.

patterns.label: Sliding window
patterns.summary: Track a contiguous part of the input, adding at its right end and removing from its left end.

patterns.label: Binary search
patterns.summary: Compare a middle candidate, then eliminate the half that cannot contain the answer.

patterns.label: Stack
patterns.summary: Process the most recently added item first, removing it from the top of the stack.

patterns.label: Monotonic stack or deque
patterns.summary: Keep stack or deque values in increasing or decreasing order by removing entries that break that order.

patterns.label: Queue simulation
patterns.summary: Add items at the back and process them from the front, in the order they arrived.

patterns.label: Heap / priority queue
patterns.summary: Keep the smallest or largest available item at the top so it can be selected as items are added and removed.

patterns.label: Quickselect partitioning
patterns.summary: Split values around a pivot, then continue only in the part containing the requested sorted position.

patterns.label: Prefix / suffix accumulation
patterns.summary: Store sums, products, or counts accumulated before or after positions so those totals can be reused.

patterns.label: Candidate cancellation
patterns.summary: Increase support for matching candidate values and cancel that support when competing values appear.

patterns.label: Value-to-index placement
patterns.summary: Place each allowed value at the array index assigned to that value, then inspect missing or repeated placements.

patterns.label: Linked-list pointer updates
patterns.summary: Save the next node before changing a link so the unprocessed list stays reachable.

patterns.label: Fast and slow pointers
patterns.summary: Move one pointer one step and another two steps to detect a cycle or identify a list position.

patterns.label: Indexed state with recency / frequency
patterns.summary: Look up entries by key and track access order or access counts to decide which entry to remove.

patterns.label: Depth-first traversal
patterns.summary: Follow one branch as far as needed before returning to explore the next branch.

patterns.label: Breadth-first traversal
patterns.summary: Use a queue to visit all nodes in the current distance layer before nodes one edge farther away.

patterns.label: Binary search tree ordering
patterns.summary: Use the rule that left-subtree values are smaller and right-subtree values are larger than a node.

patterns.label: Divide and conquer
patterns.summary: Split the input into smaller parts, solve those parts, and combine their answers.

patterns.label: Backtracking
patterns.summary: Choose an option, explore the choices after it, then undo it before trying another option.

patterns.label: Trie / prefix tree
patterns.summary: Store words along shared character-by-character paths, with markers for complete words.

patterns.label: Topological ordering
patterns.summary: Start with nodes that have no unmet prerequisites, then reduce the remaining prerequisites of their dependents.

patterns.label: Weighted path optimization
patterns.summary: Compare route costs through neighboring nodes and update a best-known cost when a cheaper route is found.

patterns.label: Minimum spanning tree
patterns.summary: Connect all graph nodes with the minimum total edge cost, without adding cycles.

patterns.label: Dynamic programming
patterns.summary: Store answers to smaller repeated problems and use those answers when computing larger ones.

patterns.label: Expand around centers
patterns.summary: Start at a character or a gap between characters and extend outward while the two sides match.

patterns.label: Greedy invariant
patterns.summary: Choose the best currently available option using a rule that keeps an optimal final answer possible.

patterns.label: Ordered interval processing
patterns.summary: Process start and end positions in order to identify overlaps, gaps, and completed intervals.

patterns.label: Arithmetic or counting identity
patterns.summary: Compute the result using arithmetic relationships, digit positions, or counting formulas.

patterns.label: Bit manipulation
patterns.summary: Inspect and change binary digits using AND, OR, XOR, masks, and shifts.

patterns.label: Eulerian edge traversal
patterns.summary: Use each graph edge once and finish a node only after its unused outgoing edges have been explored.

patterns.label: Sort candidates by priority
patterns.summary: Sort the available items by the needed priority and take the first item, repeating as the available set changes.

patterns.label: Union-find components
patterns.summary: Track each connected group by a representative, merging representatives when a new connection joins two groups.
